q: The Braverman–Yampolsky theorem on Julia sets states:
opts: The Mandelbrot set is computable, but Julia sets J(f_c) for c ∈ ∂M may be noncomputable
Julia sets are computable iff c is rational
The Julia set of z²+c is always a circle
exp: Braverman–Yampolsky (2006–2008): M is computable (one can decide membership up to ε). But for some c ∈ ∂M, the Julia set J(f_c) is not computable — no algorithm can approximate it. This shows geometric objects arising from simple dynamics can be computationally inaccessible.
